Note 1 – Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Apple Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries. Intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated. In the opinion of the Company’s management, the condensed consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments, which are normal and recurring in nature, necessary for fair financial statement presentation.
Note 2 – Revenue
Net sales disaggregated by significant products and services for the three- and nine-month periods are presented in the tables above. Total deferred revenue as of June 27, 2026 was $13.9 billion, of which the Company expects 66% to be realized in less than a year.
Note 5 – Debt

During the nine months ended June 27, 2026, the Company repaid $6.2 billion of maturing notes and issued no new notes.

Item 2.    Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
This Item and other sections of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q (“Form 10-Q”) contain forward-looking statements, within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, that involve risks and uncertainties. Forward-looking statements provide current expectations of future events based on certain assumptions and include any statement that does not directly relate to any historical or current fact. Factors that might cause such differences include, but are not limited to, those discussed in Part I, Item 1A of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 27, 2025 under the heading “Risk Factors.”
Available Information
The Company periodically provides certain information for investors on its corporate website and its investor relations website. This includes press releases and other information about financial performance, information on environmental, social and governance matters, and details related to the Company’s annual meeting of shareholders.
Business Seasonality and Product Introductions
The Company has historically experienced higher net sales in its first quarter compared to other quarters in its fiscal year due in part to seasonal holiday demand. Additionally, new product and service introductions can significantly impact net sales, cost of sales and operating expenses. The timing of product introductions can also impact the Company’s net sales to its indirect distribution channels as these channels are filled with new inventory following a product launch.
Quarterly Highlights
The Company’s total net sales increased 13% or $11.2 billion during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025, driven by higher net sales of smartphones, personal computers and services. The strength in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar had a favorable impact on the Company’s total net sales during the third quarter of 2026.
During the third quarter of 2026 the Company announced updated personal computer and tablet models and previewed the next versions of its operating systems. The Company also repurchased $23.0 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $3.9 billion during the quarter.
Macroeconomic Conditions
Macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, interest rates, tariffs and other trade measures, and currency fluctuations, have directly and indirectly impacted, and could in the future materially impact, the Company’s results of operations and financial condition. During the third quarter of 2026, tariffs on products imported into the U.S. increased the Company’s cost of sales by approximately $1.1 billion, and the Company expects a similar impact in the fourth quarter if current trade measures remain in place.
Segment Operating Performance
The following table shows net sales by reportable segment for the three months ended June 27, 2026 and June 28, 2025 (dollars in millions):

Americas net sales increased during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025 due primarily to higher net sales of smartphones and services. Europe net sales increased due primarily to higher net sales of smartphones and personal computers and the favorable impact of foreign currency. Greater China net sales increased due primarily to higher net sales of smartphones, partially offset by lower net sales of wearables.
Gross Margin
Total gross margin percentage was 47.0% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 46.6% in the same quarter of 2025. Products gross margin percentage decreased to 36.1% from 36.8% due primarily to higher tariff-related costs, partially offset by a favorable mix. Services gross margin percentage increased to 76.3% from 75.6% due primarily to a different services mix.
Operating Expenses
Research and development expense increased 11% during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025 due primarily to increases in headcount-related expenses and infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence features. Selling, general and administrative expense increased 4% due primarily to higher headcount-related expenses.
Liquidity and Capital Resources
The Company believes its balances of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond. As of June 27, 2026, the Company had $128.9 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and $93.6 billion of total term debt outstanding. The Company’s manufacturing purchase obligations were $34.6 billion, the majority of which are expected to be paid within 12 months.
Critical Accounting Estimates
There have been no material changes to the Company’s critical accounting estimates from those described in the Company’s 2025 Form 10-K.
Item 3.    Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
There have been no material changes to the Company’s market risk during the first nine months of 2026. For a discussion of the Company’s exposure to market risk, refer to the Company’s market risk disclosures set forth in Part II, Item 7A of the 2025 Form 10-K.
Item 4.    Controls and Procedures
Based on an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of the Company’s management, the Company’s principal executive officer and principal financial officer have concluded that the Company’s disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of June 27, 2026.

PART II — OTHER INFORMATION
Item 1.    Legal Proceedings
The Company is subject to legal proceedings and claims that have not been fully resolved and that have arisen in the ordinary course of business. For a discussion of the legal and regulatory risks the Company faces, see Part I, Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K under the heading “Legal and Regulatory Compliance Risks.”
Item 1A.    Risk Factors
The Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including those described in Part I, Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K under the heading “Risk Factors.” There have been no material changes to those risk factors, except that tariffs and other trade measures announced during 2026 have increased the Company’s cost of sales.
Item 2.    Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds
Purchases of Equity Securities by the Issuer and Affiliated Purchasers
Share repurchase activity during the three months ended June 27, 2026 was as follows: the Company repurchased 118 million shares for $23.0 billion under a program authorized by the Board of Directors, and $78.4 billion remained available under the program at the end of the quarter.
